query: why does taiwan use zhuyin bopomofo instead of pinyin
lead: If you learned Chinese with Pinyin, Taiwan's insistence on Zhuyin (Bopomofo) can seem puzzling — but there are real reasons behind it.
detail: Zhuyin was created in the 1910s, decades before Pinyin (1950s), and became embedded in Taiwan's schooling: children learn it first, and kids' books print it alongside characters as a reading bridge. Beyond history, its 37 non-Latin symbols keep the pronunciation aid visually separate from both English and the Chinese characters, which many teachers find gives cleaner, more accurate pronunciation. It is not that one system is right — Pinyin is the global standard for typing and international learners — but for a Taiwanese-style start, Zhuyin is the path. {name} teaches those 37 symbols the way Taiwanese children first meet them, through play, pay once and offline.
